subject: Clarify uplift fee & trial credit reconciliation for Polaris integration
messages:
From: Jodie Walker <jodie@polaris-sys.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Polaris Finance <finance@polaris-sys.com>, Trevor Li <trevor@polaris-sys.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Clarify uplift fee & trial credit reconciliation for Polaris integration

Hi Connor,

Quick note after today's rollout call — our finance team pulled the partner economics and there are two items they want clarified before we approve the first milestone invoice: the 10% reseller uplift (listed in section 3.2 of the commercial term sheet) and how you intend to apply the $15,000 trial credit Redwood granted during the pilot.

Specifically: can Redwood apply the $15k as an offset against the first invoice net-of-uplift (i.e., calculate uplift on the gross then subtract the credit), or do you compute uplift after credits are applied? Polaris prefers the former but we need a written confirmation of the calculation and the payment timeline.

Also: we had a question on lead registration — the engineering services order referenced a 45-day registration window for demo-introductions. Can you confirm whether the standard lead-protection applies to partner-introduced opportunities for integrations vs. reseller-sourced deals? That will determine how we route the first two pilot customers for co-sell credits.

Thanks,
Jodie Walker
Head of Strategic Partnerships
Polaris Systems

---
Attachments: sample_price_schedule.csv (CSV)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jodie Walker <jodie@polaris-sys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify uplift fee & trial credit reconciliation for Polaris integration

Jodie —

Thanks for the clear summary. Short answers up front: we can net the $15k trial credit against the first invoice and calculate the 10% uplift on pre-credit gross (so uplift applies to list price, then credit is deducted). That matches common reseller practice and keeps reporting consistent for both sides.

Operationally, here's what we'll do this week:
- Ben will produce an adjusted invoice showing both calculation methods (uplift-first vs. credit-first) so finance can see exact numbers.
- We'll target payment terms Net 30 from invoice date; if Polaris needs Net 45 we can note that in the invoice metadata but charges stay the same.
- On lead registration: our standard partner playbook treats "partner-introduced" integrations as partner-originated for the first 90 days post-intro for crediting and first-touch attribution. I'll include a short MAP (mutual action plan) clause for the Polaris pilot that specifically flags co-sell vs. reseller routing.

Looping in Marissa for the MAP and Ben for the invoice math. Neha — once we confirm numbers, can you add the Polaris registration to the partner portal and lock the 90-day attribution window?

Connor
Head of Alliances | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jodie Walker <jodie@polaris-sys.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T08:44:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify uplift fee & trial credit reconciliation for Polaris integration

Thanks — adding the MAP and a short guest flow so both teams have operational clarity. Key bullets for Polaris MAP (draft):
- Ownership: Polaris credited as partner-introduced for 90 days after the demo/introduction; if Polaris provides a signed PO within that window they retain first-touch credit.
- Billing reconciliation: Redwood issues an invoice with uplift applied to list price, then we apply trial credits as a separate line item. Net payable is clear on the face of the invoice.
- Disputes: finance raises disputes within 15 days of invoice receipt; disputed amounts can be placed on hold with a joint review SLA of 7 business days.
- Escalation: technical/QA issues route to our Partner CS queue; commercial disputes to alliances@redwoodinference.com.

Attached is a short MAP doc and an example flow for lead registration. Please review and we can finalize with Ben's invoice.

Marissa Cole
Partner Programs Manager
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: MAP_Polaris_intro.docx (DOCX)
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jodie Walker <jodie@polaris-sys.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Polaris Finance <finance@polaris-sys.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify uplift fee & trial credit reconciliation for Polaris integration

Hi all — attaching the draft invoice and two calculation tables so you can see the delta. Summary numbers:
- List price for milestone: $150,000
- 10% reseller uplift (applied to list): +$15,000 -> subtotal $165,000
- Trial credit: -$15,000 -> net due $150,000

If you apply the credit first and then uplift you get a slightly different net due ($148,500). We typically report uplift on gross and show credits as separate adjustments for auditability; I've included both lines in the PDF.

I've also included payment instructions and an invoice reference PO-78234. If Polaris confirms Net 45, please indicate and we'll set the payment terms accordingly before sending the final invoice.

Ben Carter
Revenue Operations 
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: invoice_POL-78234.pdf (PDF)
From: Jodie Walker <jodie@polaris-sys.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Polaris Finance <finance@polaris-sys.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T13:55:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify uplift fee & trial credit reconciliation for Polaris integration

Connor / Ben —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the side-by-side math. Polaris confirms the uplift-first approach (matches our procurement reporting) and we agree to Net 45 for this first milestone only; please annotate the invoice with Net 45 and we will process according to our payment run.

One small ask on the MAP: can Redwood remove exclusivity language for the integration pilot? We want the freedom to resell non-exclusively to demonstrate market fit. That said, the 90-day registration window is fine.

If you can send the updated invoice + a one-page MAP without exclusivity, I can countersign and route the SOW to legal for DocuSign.

Appreciate it — Jodie
